title: End quiz
intro: The same eight topics as the start quiz, with new jobs. Pick Jev, an LLM or plain Code for each one, then see how much you improved.

questions.prompt: Every night, 100,000 product reviews must be labeled positive, neutral or negative, as cheaply as possible. Which tool fits best?
questions.explanation: A typed Choice per review is fast, and Jev pays only for the tokens it reads. An LLM would pay for every token it writes, 100,000 times.

questions.prompt: Draft a short apology email that sounds human and mentions the customer's order. Which tool fits best?
questions.explanation: Jev cannot write text. Free-form writing is what an LLM is for.

questions.prompt: Count exactly how many of 12 listed items are fruit. Which tool should do the counting?
questions.explanation: Jev can judge each item as fruit or not, but counting is a calculation. Code counts the yes answers exactly.

questions.prompt: A person can review only a few answers. Which tool tells you which answers are shaky enough to review?
questions.explanation: Jev's probabilities sit near the middle when it is unsure. Review those and trust the confident ones.

questions.prompt: A manager wants to turn up how much tone matters in a review score, without asking the model again. Which tool applies the new weight?
questions.explanation: The weighted sum is plain arithmetic over Jev's stored answers, so changing a weight costs nothing and never drifts.

questions.prompt: Brainstorm ten names for a new coffee shop. Which tool fits best?
questions.explanation: Open-ended ideas need free text. Jev answers typed questions about text it is given and Code has no rule for it.

questions.prompt: A bank wants each suspicious text message checked for urgency, a fake link and a request for money, in one fast call. Which tool fits best?
questions.explanation: Several yes or no questions about one message fit in one Jev request, each with its own probability.

questions.prompt: Check that a discount code is exactly three letters followed by four digits. Which tool fits best?
questions.explanation: An exact format is a rule, and Code applies a rule perfectly. A model could be fooled by wording; a pattern check cannot.
